contribution.value: First systematic investigation showing that quantized LLMs (8-bit and 4-bit via bitsandbytes) often exhibit superior robustness than full-precision counterparts in code generation, against adversarial prompt attacks and weight noise perturbations.

ev.section: Smaller = Weaker? Benchmarking Robustness of Quantized LLMs in Code Generation
ev.quote: we present the first systematic investigation of how quantization affects the robustness of LLMs in code generation tasks
We evaluate our approach on two mainstream code generation benchmarks: HumanEval [23] and MBPP [24]. HumanEval consists of 164 Python programming problems
MBPP (Mostly Basic Programming Problems) contains 974 Python programming tasks, designed to test fundamental programming abilities
we additionally incorporate HumanEval Plus and MBPP Plus
MBPP Plus filters low-quality samples to 378 problems, so we evaluate identical samples across both versions

key_results.value: Across adversarial experiments, 51.59% of cases show quantized LLMs are more robust than originals, 42.86% favour originals, 5.56% are tied

ev.quote: 51.59% of cases show that quantized LLMs are more robust than their original versions, 42.86% of cases show that original LLMs are more robust

key_results.value: 8-bit quantization decreases clean pass@1 by only 0.36% on average; 4-bit decreases it by 1.19%

ev.quote: 8 bit quantization decreases clean performance by just 0.36% on average, while 4-bit causes a more noticeable 1.19% reduction

ev.section: Smaller = Weaker? Benchmarking Robustness of Quantized LLMs in Code Generation
ev.quote: we present the first systematic investigation of how quantization affects the robustness of LLMs in code generation tasks

strengths.value: Dual-perspective evaluation: input-level adversarial attacks (character/word/sentence) plus model-level Gaussian and Uniform weight noise.

ev.quote: input-level robustness using three types of adversarial attacks and model-level robustness through two systematic noise perturbations

strengths.value: Introduces Relative Robustness Score (RRS) that normalizes degradation between original and quantized models for fair comparison.

ev.quote: we propose the Relative Robustness Score (RRS), which directly quantifies the relationship between robustness degradation in original and quantized models

strengths.value: Open-source standardized tool released for evaluating LLM robustness pre- and post-quantization for any LLM.

ev.quote: We develop and open-source a flexible, standardized tool for evaluating LLM robustness pre- and postquantization, which is applicable to any LLM

weaknesses.value: Choice of quantization method (only bitsandbytes) may bias results compared with other quantization techniques.

ev.quote: our chosen quantization method, which could affect results differently than alternative quantization techniques

weaknesses.value: Adversarial-attack hyperparameters (e.g., 0.5 character probability, 5-char limit) may shape findings.

ev.quote: the specific parameter settings such as the character-level attack's specific transformation parameters (0.5 probability, 5-character maximum)

weaknesses.value: Construct validity threatened by metric and attack-method choices specific to code generation domain.

ev.quote: the selection of metrics used to evaluate the robustness of LMCs, as well as the methodologies employed to implement adversarial attacks

weaknesses.value: StarCoder discarded on HumanEval because the model could not produce any usable outputs in that setting.

ev.quote: FOR STARCODER, WE DISCARD IT ON HUMANEVAL DATASET SINCE WE CANNOT GET ANY OUTPUTS

limitations.value: Restricted to Python code generation; broader programming languages not yet evaluated.

ev.quote: we plan to extend this investigation with additional programming languages, model architectures, and quantization techniques

limitations.value: Only bitsandbytes NF4 and INT8 tested; sub-4-bit and other PTQ schemes (GPTQ, AWQ) not benchmarked.

ev.quote: We leverage bitsandbytes library for model quantization, which supports both 4-bit and 8-bit precision levels

limitations.value: No latency, throughput, or energy measurements; speedup or efficiency claims rely on cited bitsandbytes behaviour.
